evidence.observation: streamProxy checks `if (!response.ok)` at line 174 and throws at line 184 before it obtains a body reader (line 187) or dispatches any stream event, so a rejected request never reaches the event-processing effects. Every failure path then funnels into one stable error event: the non-OK response (line 184), a clean EOF without a terminal event (lines 236-242), and any thrown exception caught at lines 246-256 all produce `{ type: "error", reason, error: partial }` with `errorMessage` set. This is the validate-before-effect plus single-error-shape pattern the demo transfers.

The exported ProxyAssistantMessageEvent union declares exactly one `error` variant (lines 53-59), carrying a constrained `reason` (`aborted` | `error`), an optional `errorMessage`, plus `usage` and `providerThinkingLevel`. Consumers therefore have a single stable failure envelope with a closed set of fields and reasons, which is the shape the demo's AdapterError reproduces with its fixed keys and closed error-code domain.

processProxyEvent validates each delta against the content type it targets and throws a descriptive Error before mutating the partial message: `text_delta` for non-text content (line 293), `text_end` (line 307), `thinking_delta` (line 325), `thinking_end` (line 339) and `toolcall_delta` (line 365). The exhaustive `default` branch (lines 400-404) guards unknown event types. This is the same reject-before-apply ordering the demo uses when it validates params before invoking the command effect.

claims.claim: In packages/agent/src/proxy.ts, streamProxy validates the transport response before performing any stream effect: it throws on a non-OK response at line 184 before acquiring the body reader at line 187 or pushing any event, so invalid or rejected requests are refused before the effect layer runs.

streamProxy reports every kind of failure through one stable error shape, `{ type: "error", reason, error: partial }` with `errorMessage`: the non-OK HTTP response case (line 184), the missing-terminal-event EOF case (lines 236-242) and the caught-exception case (lines 246-256) all converge on it rather than surfacing distinct shapes.

ProxyAssistantMessageEvent delineates the stable failure envelope as a single `error` variant with a closed `reason` domain and an optional `errorMessage`, giving consumers one normalized error result to handle.

processProxyEvent rejects a delta that does not match its targeted content type by throwing before mutating the partial message, demonstrating the same reject-before-effect ordering used for input validation in the demo.

The demo's dispatch() mirrors the proxy pattern: it validates the request envelope, command name and params in that order and returns an AdapterError before calling any command effect, so the recorded effects array is unchanged for every rejected request.

The demo emits exactly one stable error shape, `{ type: "error", code, message, requestId }` with a closed code domain (`invalid_envelope`, `unknown_command`, `invalid_params`, `command_failed`), and normalizes even an effect that throws into that same shape, matching the single error variant of ProxyAssistantMessageEvent.

conclusion: The proxy.ts pattern transfers cleanly to a local RPC/command adapter. packages/agent/src/proxy.ts rejects a bad response at line 174/184 before it reads the body or emits events, then funnels non-OK responses, mid-stream EOF and thrown exceptions into a single `{ type: "error", reason, error }` event declared by the one error variant of ProxyAssistantMessageEvent. The demo `.prale-eval/rpc-adapter-demo.ts` applies that ordering to dispatch(): envelope, command lookup and param validation each return the one AdapterError shape before the command effect runs, so rejected input cannot produce a side effect. Running the demo executes seven scenarios (valid add, non-numeric params, missing param, unknown command, missing requestId, non-object request, throwing effect); all assertions pass and the process exits 0.

validation.notes: The dependency-free demo ran under Node v24.14.0 strip-only TypeScript mode and exited 0 with 'All demo checks passed'. It asserts that each rejected request leaves the effects array unchanged (effect not performed), that every error result has the identical key set and a code from the closed domain, and that the valid request performs exactly one effect. The repository's existing proxy test packages/agent/test/proxy.test.ts could not be run because workspace dependencies are not installed (no node_modules) and installing them is out of scope; that is the recorded validation limitation. The demo is self-contained so it validates the transferred invariants without that dependency.
